notes.title: Devlogs in yearly review - Devlog #18
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38753827/5351d43d56b3dd7203b35413f5586b94bfdeea6c.png

Hello fellow Vikings!

2023 is looming on the horizon and it's an excellent time for a little retrospection. Throughout the year we shared eleven devlogs detailing our ideas for the game and the inner workings of some systems. Have a look at the things that we’ve done.

We started  this year with specifics about gathering and processing resources from raw  materials to necessary tools. We continued this in part two, where  we focused on the end-line of production chains, which is the creation and use of high-quality items and luxury goods, along with the buildings where those will be produced, such as Smithy, Bone Carver, Jeweler or Beekeeper.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38753827/5f064d8a44a14f32d5963812729ebabe98ad48ff.gif

What piqued your interest the most? Well, obviously, swords. In our ninth article we covered the nitty-gritty of Viking ironworking. Did you know they extracted iron from bogs? It was a deep dive into historical methods to faithfully replicate them in Viking City Builder. The next logical step was showing the whole arsenal of deadly weapons from our game, both ranged and intended for melee. Including, but not limited to: seax, spear, skeggox and mighty Dane axe. Give that one good read and perhaps tell us what weapons you personally would like to see?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38753827/a86fabdcfbd619cc8eb40fb9bb30ae827036ba27.gif

However, all that work and fighting gets pretty tiresome, yet Vikings still took their leisure time seriously. Besides feasting and drinking, their activities were often a combination of fun, competition and training. Things  like arm wrestling, sparring, swimming (while trying to drown each other) or board games. They also spend time caring about hygiene, taking frequent baths and combing hair.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38753827/454cff4811da4a87fb0598d585948a2f8fb7df9f.gif

Our team also wanted to give you a sneak peek into the creative process and each department chimed in. Programmers wrote about Building System Roles, while artists presented processes of creating animations, preparing sounds and converting 2D to 3D while making the UI of the main menu.

If you haven't seen this year's devlogs yet, we encourage you to catch up!
- Creating animations in Viking City Builder - Devlog #7,
- Raw materials part I - Devlog #8,
- From swamp to sword! - Devlog #9, 
- Tools of War – Devlog #10,
- Vikings and their clothes - Devlog #11,
- Vikings free time – Devlog #12,
- System of building roles – Devlog #13,
- Working on Main Menu - Devlog #14,
- Variety of buildings and decorations - Devlog #15,
- Implementation of sounds – Devlog #16,
- Raw materials part II – Devlog #17.

We hope you enjoyed all of them! Thank you for being with us and we can promise that next year we won’t slow down and will show even more!

Also, don't forget to join our Discord, where we keep you updated on everything.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38753827/2724474b3f8a17c90fc924bcb14e6935f4553e22.gif

notes.title: Raw materials part I - Devlog #8
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38753827/18ff1c27e0d384ef9fbe0ad9526a861389e88a29.png

Greetings fellow Vikings! 

This part of the devlog will be devoted to the mechanics describing collection and processing of collected resources. From basic and vital resources to fancy and rarest materials like Damascus steel, our development team strives to reflect the real conditions and methods that the Vikings used to obtain and process their materials.

The design of each of the production chains is preceded by an in-depth historical research. Thanks to many hours spent with various historical sources, we can faithfully reproduce the entire process - of course, as much as the game mechanics allow us to ;)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38753827/d014ef79fec858556e6ea4dc304ab3658650b9dc.png

From obtaining the resource to creation of the final product, the entire procedure has been carefully designed to reflect the spirit of a functioning Viking settlement as closely as possible.

All sources of the materials obtained during the game are based on the actual deposits that existed at that time. For example, bog iron, essential for the production of iron, is mined in swamps as it was in reality. Of course, all deposits have a limited amount of resources they contain, and their availability and abundance of minerals depends on the map on which the game is played. For example, a settlement built on the "Birka" map will offer easier access to water and more building space than the mountainous "Kaupang" area, which in turn is richer in stone deposits. Sometimes players aiming to gather specific resources will need to work in various ways like trading or plundering.

The player will be able to adapt his playstyle to the conditions on the map. The selection of appropriate production chains, control over the resource flow and use of available raw materials will allow for the effective utilization of the riches ​​of each area.

The resources available in the game can be divided into several categories in terms of their purpose and rarity. The first category will be food, which includes both basic products obtained in the first stages of the game, such as mushrooms or blackberries, to items that require production, such as bread or mead. This category also includes all commodities required to produce food, such as wheat.

[previewyoutube=DCGnW8yrXcg;full][/previewyoutube]

Building materials are another category of raw resources. Starting with the basic ones, such as clay, wood or stone, and ending with those requiring production, such as iron, which is also an industrial resource - used in the production of various goods.

Industrial items and resources, such as the aforementioned iron, will serve in the production chains as required elements to create a finished product.

Luxury goods and armaments, both weapons and armor, make up the bundle of end products on which the resource processing chain closes. Thus, in the simplest way, the production of goods can be represented in several steps: obtaining raw materials - processing raw materials - creating a product.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38753827/d014ef79fec858556e6ea4dc304ab3658650b9dc.png

Introducing you to the whole range of developer tasks that make up the design of the above-mentioned production chains, the following stages of work are presented:

1. Research on historical sources - the first point of design. Here we check how the processing of a specific resource looked like in the times of the Vikings.

2. Next comes creating the basic logic simulation: 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38753827/a6f7d4be08f0b3ab1c11ed2b2bc6eba1fd14c467.png

After that we implement the idea on the model and tweak the mechanics to fit in our game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38753827/2724474b3f8a17c90fc924bcb14e6935f4553e22.gif

Thank you for your interest in seeing how the resource design process works! We hope that the material was interesting and brought you a little closer to the details of working on Viking City Builder.

notes.title: [FAQ] - Answers to your questions
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38753827/c740a8d4c6b5ff1efbef48f9be66221f5ad837e3.png

Hello, Vikings! I’ve collected the most frequently asked questions about Viking City Builder. Read through and make sure there isn't an issue here that you would like to ask about. Stay tuned!

When will the game be released?
Unfortunately, at this point in the development process, I can't say exactly, when the game will be released. I’m doing my best to make it happen as soon as possible. Stay tuned!

How much will that game cost?
I’ll be able to tell you the price of the game a moment before its release. 

Is it true that only one person is working on Viking City Builder?
Of course, it’s true. I wish I had a big team to finish this game quicker, but I’m an indie developer, so I have to do the best I can. I'm using some assets from a marketplace to speed up the development, which is a common practice in Indie Games.

What platforms will this game be available on?
I plan to release the game on PC and you will be able to buy it on Steam. I'm also considering a console version.

Will the game have any demo/prologue? If so, will it be free?
I can assure you that such a demo or prologue will be released and it will be for free.

Will there be beta testing? If so, how will it be possible to apply to them?
At this point, I'm not looking for anyone to test, but as soon as the opportunity arises I'll be sure to let you know via my social media.

What engine was used in the game?
Unreal Engine was used in the game.

Will there be a multiplayer mode in the game?
At this point, I have no plans to introduce a multiplayer mode in Viking City Builder.

Does the game have its Discord server?
Not yet, but don't worry, the game will definitely have Discord.

Helmets with horns?
Next to the release date, this is probably one of the most frequently asked questions. So. . . To answer: why helmets with horns? As a big fan of Norse mythology and Viking culture, I have to admit that your comments are correct that the image of a Viking wearing a helmet with horns is not historically accurate. I’ve used it so the people instantly recognize the vikings on the screenshots and videos, and the horned helmets are very recognizable. But in the final version of the game I’d love to be true to historical sources and find other ways to convey the Viking spirit.

Why did you use music from Mount & Blade: Warband - Viking Conquest?
I bought the music for the trailer from a paid soundtrack site. Link: HERE.

Is there any way I can support your work?
Adding my game to your list is the biggest support for me because it increases its visibility on Steam. If you haven't already done so, I'd love it if you added it. This will help me a lot on my way to releasing the game.

Where can I find more information about the game?
More information about ‘Viking City Builder’ you can find on Steam and my social media, links below: 
- Facebook,
- Instagram,
- Twitter,
- YouTube.

Is this game a fake?
Not sure, let you decide… 

P.S. I'm working on my first devblog:
